pages.title: About Our Kitchen
pages.content:
Hearth & Herb is our family kitchen table, opened up to anyone who wants to pull up a chair. We are two parents, three children and a very hopeful dog, cooking real food on real weeknights.

What we believe

  • Dinner does not need to be fancy to be special.
  • Good ingredients and a hot pan beat complicated techniques.
  • Everyone helps, even if it is just setting the table.

How we test

Every recipe is cooked at least three times in our ordinary kitchen with ordinary pans. If a step can go wrong, we tell you how to fix it.

The best meals are the ones where nobody checks their phone.

House rule

posts.title: One-Pan Lemon & Herb Chicken Thighs
posts.excerpt: Crispy-skinned chicken, soft potatoes and charred lemon, all roasted in one pan. Our most-cooked Tuesday dinner.
posts.content:
If our family has a signature dish, this is it. Everything goes into one heavy pan, the oven does the work, and twenty minutes later the kitchen smells of lemon, garlic and thyme.

Bone-in thighs are forgiving: they stay juicy even if dinner runs late, and the skin crisps beautifully. The potatoes cook underneath and soak up all the pan juices.

Start skin-side down

Brown the thighs on the hob before they go in the oven. It takes six extra minutes and gives you shatteringly crisp skin.

Swaps that work

  • Use sweet potatoes or squash instead of potatoes.
  • Swap thyme for rosemary or oregano.
  • Add a tin of drained chickpeas for the last fifteen minutes.

One-pan lemon & herb chicken

  • Prep15 min
  • Cook40 min
  • Serves4
  • CostBudget

Ingredients

  • 8 bone-in chicken thighs
  • 750 g small potatoes, halved
  • 2 lemons, one sliced, one juiced
  • 6 garlic cloves, unpeeled
  • A small bunch of thyme
  • 3 tbsp olive oil
  • Salt and pepper

Method

  1. Heat the oven to 210°C.
  2. Season the chicken and brown it skin-side down in an ovenproof pan.
  3. Lift out the chicken, add potatoes, garlic and lemon slices and toss in the fat.
  4. Return the chicken, skin up, and scatter over the thyme.
  5. Roast for 35–40 minutes until golden and cooked through.
  6. Squeeze over the lemon juice and serve from the pan.

Leftovers make brilliant sandwiches the next day with a spoon of mayonnaise.

Print recipe

comments.author: Bridget
comments.content: This is on repeat in our house. The kids fight over the crispy potatoes.

comments.author: Owen
comments.content: Made it with drumsticks and it worked just as well.

posts.title: Smoky White Bean & Kale Soup
posts.excerpt: A thick, smoky pot of beans, greens and tomatoes that tastes like it simmered all day. It takes thirty-five minutes.
posts.content:
When the evenings draw in, this soup is on our stove at least once a week. Smoked paprika gives it depth without any meat, and mashing a few of the beans makes it creamy.

It is a pantry rescue too: tinned beans, tinned tomatoes, an onion and whatever greens are wilting in the drawer.

Soup is just a pot of patience. This one needs very little.

Grandma Ruth

Make it ahead

The soup thickens overnight, so add a splash of water or stock when you reheat it. It freezes well for up to three months.

Smoky white bean & kale soup

  • Prep10 min
  • Cook25 min
  • Serves6
  • Freezes3 months

Ingredients

  • 2 tbsp olive oil
  • 1 onion, 2 carrots, 2 celery sticks, chopped
  • 3 garlic cloves
  • 2 tsp smoked paprika
  • 2 tins cannellini beans
  • 1 tin chopped tomatoes
  • 1 litre vegetable stock
  • 150 g kale, shredded

Method

  1. Soften the onion, carrot and celery in the oil for 8 minutes.
  2. Stir in the garlic and paprika for 1 minute.
  3. Add beans, tomatoes and stock and simmer for 15 minutes.
  4. Mash a quarter of the beans against the side of the pot.
  5. Stir in the kale and cook for 3 minutes more.
  6. Season well and serve with bread.
Print recipe

comments.author: Priya
comments.content: Added a parmesan rind while it simmered. So good.

posts.title: No-Knead Rosemary Loaf
posts.excerpt: Four ingredients, five minutes of work and a long, lazy rise. The crackly loaf we bake every Saturday.
posts.content:
You do not need a stand mixer, a starter or strong arms to bake good bread. This dough is stirred together the night before and left alone while you sleep.

Baking it in a lidded pot traps the steam, which is the secret to a blistered, crackly crust at home.

What you need

  • A large bowl and a spoon
  • A heavy pot with a lid that can go in a hot oven
  • Baking paper
  • Time, mostly

No-knead rosemary loaf

  • Prep5 min
  • Rise12–18 hr
  • Bake45 min
  • Makes1 loaf

Ingredients

  • 450 g bread flour
  • 1/4 tsp instant yeast
  • 10 g salt
  • 350 ml lukewarm water
  • 2 sprigs rosemary, chopped

Method

  1. Stir everything together into a shaggy dough.
  2. Cover and leave at room temperature overnight.
  3. Tip onto a floured surface and fold into a ball.
  4. Rest on baking paper while the pot heats in a 240°C oven.
  5. Bake covered for 30 minutes, then uncovered for 15.
  6. Cool for an hour before slicing, if you can.
Print recipe

Once you have the rhythm, play with it: swap a third of the flour for wholemeal, fold in olives or a handful of seeds, or leave out the rosemary for a plain sandwich loaf.

posts.title: Sunday Pot Roast with Root Vegetables
posts.excerpt: Beef braised low and slow with carrots, onions and a glass of red until it falls apart at the touch of a fork.
posts.content:
Sunday afternoons in our house have a smell, and it is this. The pot goes in after lunch and by the time everyone wanders back from the park, dinner is ready.

Cheaper cuts like chuck or brisket are perfect here. Long, gentle cooking turns them meltingly tender.

Leftover ideas

  • Shred into tacos with pickled onions.
  • Stir into a pie filling with the leftover gravy.
  • Pile into toasted rolls with horseradish.

Use a pot that just fits the meat, so the liquid comes halfway up the sides.

If the sauce is thin at the end, simmer it uncovered for ten minutes.

Sunday pot roast

  • Prep20 min
  • Cook3 hr 30
  • Serves6
  • LevelEasy

Ingredients

  • 1.5 kg beef chuck
  • 2 onions, quartered
  • 6 carrots, in chunks
  • 4 garlic cloves
  • 2 tbsp tomato paste
  • 250 ml red wine
  • 500 ml beef stock
  • Bay leaves and thyme

Method

  1. Heat the oven to 150°C.
  2. Brown the beef well on all sides; set aside.
  3. Soften onions and garlic, stir in tomato paste.
  4. Pour in wine and stock, add herbs and return the beef.
  5. Cover and braise for 3 hours, adding carrots after 2.
  6. Rest for 15 minutes before pulling apart.
Print recipe

comments.author: Malcolm
comments.content: Smelled amazing all afternoon. Served it with mash.

posts.title: Twenty-Minute Garden Pesto Pasta
posts.excerpt: A blender pesto made with whatever herbs are growing, tossed with pasta, green beans and potatoes the Ligurian way.
posts.content:
Our herb pots overflow by August, and this is how we keep up. Basil is classic, but a mix of basil, parsley and a little mint is just as good.

Cooking potatoes and green beans in the same pot as the pasta is a trick from the Italian coast. It makes the dish heartier and saves washing up.

Pesto, our way

  1. Toast the nuts until fragrant; walnuts and sunflower seeds both work.
  2. Blitz herbs, garlic and nuts first, then add cheese.
  3. Stream in the oil last and stop while it still has texture.

Garden pesto pasta

  • Prep10 min
  • Cook12 min
  • Serves4
  • LevelEasy

Ingredients

  • 400 g pasta
  • 2 small potatoes, diced
  • 150 g green beans
  • 60 g basil and parsley
  • 1 garlic clove
  • 40 g toasted nuts
  • 50 g grated hard cheese
  • 100 ml olive oil

Method

  1. Boil the potatoes for 4 minutes, then add the pasta.
  2. Add the beans for the final 4 minutes.
  3. Blitz the herbs, garlic, nuts, cheese and oil.
  4. Drain, keeping a cup of the water.
  5. Toss everything together, loosening with the water.
Print recipe

Any leftover pesto keeps for a week in a jar with a layer of oil on top. We stir it into soups, spread it on toast and spoon it over roast vegetables.

posts.title: Skillet Eggs with Peppers & Tomatoes
posts.excerpt: Eggs gently poached in a spiced pepper and tomato sauce. Breakfast, lunch or a Thursday night dinner.
posts.content:
When the fridge is nearly empty, there are usually still eggs, an onion and a tin of tomatoes. That is all you need for this skillet.

The sauce can be as mild or as fiery as you like. We keep it gentle for the kids and pass round chilli flakes at the table.

Cover the pan

A lid traps the heat so the whites set before the yolks overcook. Check after five minutes.

Skillet eggs with peppers

  • Prep10 min
  • Cook25 min
  • Serves4
  • CostBudget

Ingredients

  • 1 onion, 2 peppers, sliced
  • 2 garlic cloves
  • 1 tsp cumin, 1 tsp paprika
  • 2 tins chopped tomatoes
  • 6 eggs
  • Parsley, feta and bread to serve

Method

  1. Soften the onion and peppers for 10 minutes.
  2. Add garlic and spices, then the tomatoes.
  3. Simmer for 10 minutes until thick.
  4. Make wells and crack in the eggs.
  5. Cover and cook for 5–7 minutes.
  6. Scatter with herbs and feta.
Print recipe

comments.author: Lena
comments.content: We had this for dinner and breakfast the same weekend.

posts.title: Apple & Blackberry Oat Crumble
posts.excerpt: Tart apples and hedgerow blackberries under a buttery oat crumble. Serve with custard, cream or a scoop of ice cream.
posts.content:
Blackberry picking is a family outing every September, and this crumble is the reward. Purple fingers, scratched arms and a bubbling dish on the table.

Oats and a little demerara sugar give the topping crunch. I always make double and keep half in the freezer for next time.

Crumble rules

  • Do not press the topping down; scatter it loosely.
  • Leave a few gaps so the fruit can bubble through.
  • Rest for ten minutes so the juices thicken.

Apple & blackberry crumble

  • Prep20 min
  • Bake40 min
  • Serves6
  • FreezesYes

Ingredients

  • 4 cooking apples, chopped
  • 250 g blackberries
  • 2 tbsp sugar
  • 150 g plain flour
  • 75 g oats
  • 100 g cold butter
  • 75 g demerara sugar

Method

  1. Heat the oven to 190°C.
  2. Toss the fruit with the sugar in a baking dish.
  3. Rub the butter into the flour, then stir in oats and demerara.
  4. Scatter over the fruit.
  5. Bake for 35–40 minutes until golden and bubbling.
Print recipe

Leftovers, if there are any, are wonderful cold for breakfast with a spoonful of thick yogurt. Nobody in our house has ever complained.

posts.title: Stocking a Pantry for Easy Weeknights
posts.excerpt: The jars, tins and bottles we never run out of, and how they turn into dinner on the busiest nights.
posts.content:
Most weeknight dinners in our kitchen start in the cupboard, not the fridge. A well-stocked pantry is the difference between cooking and ordering in.

This is not a list of fancy ingredients. It is the short, hardworking list we restock every fortnight.

Our pantry list

Tins & jars

  • Chopped tomatoes
  • Beans and chickpeas
  • Coconut milk
  • Anchovies or capers

Dry goods

  • Pasta in two shapes
  • Rice and lentils
  • Oats
  • Bread flour

Flavour

  • Smoked paprika and cumin
  • Stock cubes
  • Soy sauce
  • Good olive oil

Once a month we cook a “pantry week”, using up what is open before buying more. It keeps the shelves fresh and saves real money.

A full pantry is a promise to your future, tired self.

Kitchen wisdom

comments.author: Ade
comments.content: Pantry week is a brilliant idea. Stealing it.
